summary.intent: Commit a GSD (Get Shit Done) framework update to the cipher-box repo, cleaning up unnecessary artifacts and fixing lint ignore paths in the process.
summary.outcome: Migration journal was unstaged, deleted from disk, and added to .gitignore; .markdownlintignore was updated for new GSD paths; changes were committed on a chore/update-gsd branch, though the commit required working around a pnpm PATH issue and 1Password signing.

repo: Repo rules block direct pushes to main — PRs required for all changes.
The GSD installer uses gsd-install-state.json (not the migration journal) to track applied migrations; the journal is a rollback safety net only and is safe to gitignore.
Pre-commit hooks require pnpm, which is managed via corepack and not always on PATH in sandboxed shells.
Git commit signing is configured via 1Password, requiring an unsandboxed shell to sign commits.

code.finding: Migration journal rollback logic lives here; journal cleanup is explicitly best-effort, so a missing journal won't break future installs.

workflow: GSD migration journals are 2.9MB snapshots of pre-update state — redundant in a git-tracked repo and should be gitignored.
corepack can shim pnpm into ~/.local/bin when pnpm is not on PATH: `corepack enable pnpm`.
When a stale local branch matches main exactly with no remote, it can be reused directly without rebasing.

friction: pnpm not on PATH in the sandboxed shell caused the first commit attempt to fail via pre-commit hook.
1Password-based git commit signing required dropping sandbox mode to succeed.
Stale chore/update-gsd branch already existed locally, requiring inspection before reuse.
open_items: PR still needs to be opened from chore/update-gsd to main — the transcript ends at the commit step.
Unclear whether gsd-pristine directory purpose was ever fully explained to the user (question was noted but answer deferred).
